That is with every regime's growth spread × 1.5, the one number fitted on these outcomes (and used here): as the hidden Markov model estimates them, the range held 68% (18% below, 14% above) — a single year's regime spread understates how far revenue can drift over several.

methods.formula: Value = (assets in place + C − net debt) ÷ shares;  C = S·N(d₁) − K·e^(−rT)·N(d₂), d₁ = [ln(S ÷ K) + (r + σ²/2)T] ÷ σ√T, d₂ = d₁ − σ√T
steps: S = the expansion in year 5: the revenue it adds $17.58B (to $38.35B) × margin 40.8% × (1 − tax), as a growing perpetuity, discounted = $41.90B
K = capital to build it: $17.58B ÷ sales-to-capital 0.84 = $20.82B
σ = 41% (its stock, a year of daily closes), T = 5 years, r = 4.91% → C = $27.38B
assets in place = NOPAT $7.41B ÷ WACC = $71.76B; value = ($71.76B + $27.38B − net debt $5.41B) ÷ 921,000,000 = $101.77
